::: {#exr-miller-taylor-cube-root}
#### Taylor expansion of a fractional power

Find the first three terms of the Taylor series for

$$f(x) = (1 + x)^{1/3}$$

at $x_0 = 1/2$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-taylor-cube-root}
At $x_0 = 1/2$, $1 + x_0 = 3/2$:

$$\ba
f(1/2) &= \paren{\frac{3}{2}}^{1/3}
\\
f'(x) &= \frac{1}{3}(1 + x)^{-2/3} \implies f'(1/2) = \frac{1}{3}\paren{\frac{3}{2}}^{-2/3} = \frac{1}{3}\paren{\frac{2}{3}}^{2/3}
\\
f''(x) &= -\frac{2}{9}(1 + x)^{-5/3} \implies f''(1/2) = -\frac{2}{9}\paren{\frac{3}{2}}^{-5/3} = -\frac{2}{9}\paren{\frac{2}{3}}^{5/3}
\ea$$

Dividing $f''(1/2)$ by $2!$ gives $-\frac{1}{9}\paren{\frac{2}{3}}^{5/3}$. The Taylor polynomial is:

$$P_2(x) = \paren{\frac{3}{2}}^{1/3} + \frac{1}{3}\paren{\frac{2}{3}}^{2/3}\paren{x - \frac{1}{2}} - \frac{1}{9}\paren{\frac{2}{3}}^{5/3}\paren{x - \frac{1}{2}}^2$$
:::
